name: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
charge: Going to the king for Jeremiah, and drawing him up out of the dungeon with old cast clouts and rotten rags
summary: The princes had put Jeremiah in a dungeon of mire to die. A eunuch of the king's house, an Ethiopian, went out to Zedekiah at the gate and told him the prophet was likely to die of hunger where he was. The king gave him thirty men and he drew Jeremiah up with rags under his armholes. Before the city fell the Lord sent him his own word: thy life for a prey, because thou hast put thy trust in me.
offense: Ebed-melech, the Ethiopian eunuch in the king's house, heard that Jeremiah had been lowered into the dungeon and was sinking in the mire. He went to the king and plainly called the princes' action evil, warning that the prophet would die where he had been cast. With the king's permission, he took men and ropes to draw Jeremiah out. He also gathered old cast clouts and rotten rags and instructed Jeremiah to place them under his arms beneath the cords. His intervention joined courage before authority with careful treatment of the man being rescued.

offenseFull: Ebed-melech, the Ethiopian eunuch in the king's house, heard that Jeremiah had been lowered into the dungeon and was sinking in the mire. He went to the king and plainly called the princes' action evil, warning that the prophet would die where he had been cast.

With the king's permission, he took men and ropes to draw Jeremiah out. He also gathered old cast clouts and rotten rags and instructed Jeremiah to place them under his arms beneath the cords. His intervention joined courage before authority with careful treatment of the man being rescued.
judgmentFull: While Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison, the Lord sent him a promise for Ebed-melech. The announced evil would come upon Jerusalem, but Ebed-melech would not be delivered into the hands of the men he feared. God would deliver him, and his life would be for a prey because he had put his trust in the Lord.
The approaching fall of the city did not prevent God from distinguishing the man who trusted Him. Ebed-melech's place in the royal household did not keep him silent when its princes acted wickedly.

verses.text: Therefore the princes said unto the king, We beseech thee, let this man be put to death: for thus he weakeneth the hands of the men of war that remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words unto them: for this man seeketh not the welfare of this people, but the hurt.
Then Zedekiah the king said, Behold, he is in your hand: for the king is not he that can do any thing against you.

Then took they Jeremiah, and cast him into the dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech, that was in the court of the prison: and they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire.
Now when Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon; the king then sitting in the gate of Benjamin;
Ebed–melech went forth out of the king’s house, and spake to the king, saying,

My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the dungeon; and he is like to die for hunger in the place where he is: for there is no more bread in the city.
Then the king commanded Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.

So Ebed–melech took the men with him, and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took thence old cast clouts and old rotten rags, and let them down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah.
And Ebed–melech the Ethiopian said unto Jeremiah, Put now these old cast clouts and rotten rags under thine armholes under the cords. And Jeremiah did so.
So they drew up Jeremiah with cords, and took him up out of the dungeon: and Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
Now the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the prison, saying,

Go and speak to Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.
But I will deliver thee in that day, saith the Lord: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid.
For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the Lord.
If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;

If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.
Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the Lord, speak, saying, The Lord hath utterly separated me from his people: neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree.
For thus saith the Lord unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and take hold of my covenant;
Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off.

entries.commentary: Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashur hear Jeremiah telling the people that whoever remains in the city shall die by sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes forth to the Chaldeans shall live and have his life for a prey. The princes tell the king that Jeremiah must be put to death because he weakens the hands of the men of war and seeks not the welfare of the people but their hurt; the king answers that he is in their hand and the king can do nothing against them. They cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison, letting him down with cords into a place with no water but mire, and Jeremiah sinks in the mire.

Abedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, hears that Jeremiah has been put in the dungeon while the king sits in the gate of Benjamin. Abedmelech goes to the king and says these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah, who is likely to die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city; the king commands him to take thirty men and lift the prophet out before he dies. Abedmelech takes old cast clouts and rotten rags, lets them down by cords, and tells Jeremiah to put them under his armholes under the cords; they draw him up out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison.

Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken. The king swears secretly that as the Most High liveth he will not put him to death nor give him into the hand of those who seek his life. Jeremiah tells him that if he goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned, but if he will not go forth the city shall be given to the Chaldeans and burned; the king says he is afraid of the Jews already fallen to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah urges him to obey the voice of the Most High that it may be well with him.

If the king refuses to go forth, Jeremiah shows him that all the women left in the king's house shall be brought out to the king of Babylon's princes, saying his friends have prevailed against him and his feet are sunk in the mire and turned away back. All his wives and children shall be brought to the Chaldeans, and he shall not escape but be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon and cause the city to be burned with fire. Zedekiah charges Jeremiah to let no man know their words, and to tell the princes only that he presented his supplication not to be returned to Jonathan's house; the princes come and ask, Jeremiah answers as the king commanded, and he abides in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem is taken.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar and all his army come against Jerusalem and besiege it, and in the eleventh year, the fourth month, the ninth day, the city is broken up. The princes of the king of Babylon come in and sit in the middle gate; when Zedekiah and the men of war see them, they flee by night by the way of the king's garden through the gate between the two walls toward the plain. The Chaldean army pursues and overtakes Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and they bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where the king of Babylon slays Zedekiah's sons and all the nobles of Judah before his eyes, then puts out Zedekiah's eyes, binds him with chains for Babylon, and burns the king's house and the houses of the people, breaking down the walls of Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carries away captive to Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, those who fell away to him, and the rest, but leaves the poor of the people who had nothing in the land of Judah and gives them vineyards and fields. Nebuchadnezzar gives charge concerning Jeremiah that he be taken, looked to well, and done no harm, but treated as he himself shall say. The princes of Babylon send and take Jeremiah out of the court of the prison and commit him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to carry him home, so he dwells among the people.

While Jeremiah is still shut up in the court of the prison, the word of the Most High comes to him for Abedmelech the Ethiopian, declaring that He will bring His words upon this city for evil and not for good, and they shall be accomplished in that day. But in that day He will deliver Abedmelech, who shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, and shall not fall by the sword, because he has put his trust in the Most High; the Most High deals with the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah, sent to take the prophet up out of the dungeon before he died. -

Be not envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them, for their heart studies destruction and their lips talk of mischief. Through wisdom a house is built, by understanding it is established, and by knowledge the chambers are filled with precious and pleasant riches.

A wise man is strong; a man of knowledge increases strength. By wise counsel you make your war, and in the multitude of counselors there is safety. Something other nations use that black people have not figured out yet starts with an "m": mentorship. People freestyle without a plan and it does not work out. Other nations have mentors who already accomplished what they are trying to do and get counsel, which is advice, on how to reach that level. Some black people are too prideful to ask for help. Wisdom is too high for a fool; he opens not his mouth in the gate.

He that devises to do evil will be called a mischievous person. The thought of foolishness is sin, and the scorner is an abomination to men. The thought of foolishness is sin. We have thoughts we cannot control that pop up, and we have to rebuke them and say that is the devil. All of us have some perverse thoughts, and you have to rebuke them. If you faint in the day of adversity your strength is small.

If you forbear to deliver them that are drawn to death and ready to be slain, and say you knew it not, does not he that ponders the heart consider it and render to every man according to his works? Eat honey because it is good, and the honeycomb which is sweet; so is the knowledge of wisdom to your soul. When you find it there is a reward and your expectation will not be cut off. Cherish knowledge, wisdom, and understanding. Always be in a position to learn and see the lessons in life. Often a regular situation holds a life lesson and you miss it because your antennas are not up.

Lay not wait against the dwelling of the righteous, for a just man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked fall into mischief. Certain brothers come into the truth and make mistakes, but each mistake they learn from and rise up again. He respects brothers who make mistakes and get back in the fight, unlike those too embarrassed to admit they were wrong who run like a little girl. Rejoice not when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbles, lest the Most High see it and turn away his wrath from him.

Fret not yourself because of evil men, neither be envious of the wicked, for there is no reward to the evil man and the candle of the wicked will be put out. Whatever the wicked have going on, or riches gotten by wickedness, do not stress over it. The Most High is going to judge them and deal with them, so keep it moving. Fear the Most High and the king, and meddle not with them given to change, for their calamity rises suddenly.

It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment. He that says to the wicked, you are righteous, the people will curse and nations abhor him, but to them that rebuke him will be delight and a good blessing. Every man will kiss his lips that gives a right answer.

Prepare your work outside and make it fit in the field, and afterward build your house. Be not a witness against your neighbor without cause, and deceive not with your lips. Say not, I will do to him as he has done to me. This is where turning the other cheek comes from; you have to take the high road instead of getting vengeance. His neighbor drunkenly scratched his car while parking her sister's car, and it took everything in him not to get revenge. He let it go and took the high road.

He went by the field of the slothful and the vineyard of the man void of understanding, and it was all grown over with thorns and nettles, its stone wall broken down. He considered it well and received instruction: yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep, so your poverty comes as one that travels and your want as an armed man. These chapters deal with wisdom, raising children, avoiding sin, and laziness. These are things we need to put into our character. Proverbs is a very good character-building book that should be read often. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement)

Five were wise and five were foolish. The foolish took their lamps and took no oil with them; the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. The oil is the wisdom of the scriptures. The foolish come afterward saying, Lord, Lord, open to us, and are answered, Verily I say unto you, I know you not. Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

Every man received according to his several ability, and the two who traded were told, Well done, thou good and faithful servant. The one who hid his talent blamed his lord and called him a hard man, and was answered, Thou wicked and slothful servant. That fearful spirit is not of the Most High, and a man should examine himself for it. Unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. Knowledge that is not used is knowledge that is lost.

He separates them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats, and says to those on the right hand, Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Meeting the need of a brother or sister in the body is counted as done to Christ himself. Those on the left hand are answered with the same measure: inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Keep judgment and do justice, for His salvation is near to come and His righteousness to be revealed. Blessed is the man that does this and lays hold on it, that keeps the Sabbath from polluting it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.

The son of the stranger that has joined himself to the Most High is not to say the Lord has utterly separated him from His people, and the eunuch is not to say he is a dry tree. These strangers spoken of are Israel; the whole passage is the Most High speaking to Israel. To the eunuchs that keep His Sabbaths and take hold of His covenant, He gives a place and a name in His house better than of sons and daughters, an everlasting name that will not be cut off. The sons of the stranger that join themselves to Him, keep the Sabbath, and take hold of His covenant, He will bring to His holy mountain and make joyful in His house of prayer; their offerings will be accepted, for His house will be called a house of prayer for all people. The Lord God who gathers the outcasts of Israel says He will yet gather others to Him besides those already gathered.

All the beasts of the field and forest are called to devour. Judgment is turned on the failed leadership. The watchmen are blind and ignorant, dumb dogs that cannot bark, sleeping and loving to slumber. They are greedy dogs that never have enough, shepherds that cannot understand. They all look to their own way, every one for his gain, saying they will fetch wine and fill themselves with strong drink, and tomorrow will be as this day and much more abundant.
